title: Support ticket JSON encoding and decoding
name: Ticket JSON handlers

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how tickets are decoded from requests or encoded into responses? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client sends PATCH /tickets/7 with the body {"status":"SOLVED"}. What happens?
choices: 200, and the stored status becomes solved; the response shows "status":"solved"
200, but the status is unchanged because the value does not match exactly
500, because json.Unmarshal cannot decode into a pointer to an int-based type

questions.prompt: A client sends POST /tickets with {"subject":"Login fails","priority":3}. What does the handler do?
choices: 201; the unknown priority field is silently ignored
400; decodeStrict fails because DisallowUnknownFields rejects the field
201; priority is stored in the ticket as an extra attribute
400; json.Decoder rejects numbers that are not declared as float64

questions.prompt: A ticket is created with {"subject":"Refund"} (no tags, no due date) and then fetched with GET. What does the JSON response contain for tags, assignee_id and due_at?
choices: The keys tags, assignee_id and due_at are all omitted
